_: Text of the README harness figure (v2/where-chock-sits.png) and of the session-path figure in docs/architecture.md (v2/session-path.png); both read by their .mjs. 'points' are the 12 agentseam events (agentseam.contract.EVENTS) plus the five other places Chock acts or could; 'on' is the harness card a point sits on, 'place' where the session-path draws it; 'acts' is true where shipped Chock code acts on the point (filled badge or diamond). tests assert the agentseam points equal agentseam.contract.EVENTS, the acting set equals what the engine handles, and that no two shapes of either layout intersect. 'proof' lists the tests that prove each acting point.

points.name: Session start

points.name: Prompt submitted
points.line: judges the prompt where the agent can refuse one. Witnessed live in Claude Code. Untested in other clients.

points.label: instructions
points.name: Instructions loaded

points.label: pre-compact
points.name: Before context is compacted
points.line: agentseam exposes this point; no shipped Chock code acts on it.

points.label: pre-tool
points.name: Before a tool runs
points.line: Chock judges the call: allow, ask or block. A refusal goes back to the model with one line on what to do instead.

points.label: post-tool
points.name: After a tool runs
points.line: records what ran, for checks that read the session. It never changes a verdict.

points.label: tool failure
points.name: After a tool fails
points.line: records the failed call the same way.

points.label: file changed
points.name: A file changes

points.label: stop
points.name: End of the turn
points.line: reads what the turn left in the working tree and refuses to end the turn on a finding. A backstop.

points.label: rules
points.name: Rules in context
points.line: a short rules block Chock writes into AGENTS.md. Advisory.

harness.title: Inside a coding agent's harness, and where Chock plugs in.

key.acts: Chock runs here: a local program, rules are files in your repository, no model, no tokens
key.exposed: a hook your own policy can use

harness.alt: A coding agent's harness drawn as component cards in three layers: input (you, the prompt, the session), core (context, the agent loop and the model) and execution (the tool gate, tools, external tools over MCP and subagents), with arrows showing how they talk to each other, beside the repository and pipeline (git commit, git push, CI, main branch). Small diamonds on each card are the hooks on that component: filled where Chock runs today, hollow where a policy of your own can run. The model has none, because Chock never touches it.

path.title: A session, step by step. Chock runs at the marked points.

steps.text: The model picks the next action

steps.sub: edit a file, run a command, git

key.acts: Chock runs here: a local program, rules are files in your repository, no model, no tokens
key.exposed: a hook your own policy can use

path.alt: A session as an ordered path with checkpoints. Inside your agent: you open a session, type a request, the agent loads its rules, the model picks the next action, a tool runs (repeating until done) and the agent ends its turn; then in your repository: git commit, git push, CI on the pull request and the main branch. Diamonds on the arrows are the hook points: filled where Chock runs today (session start, rules, before and after a tool, stop, the MCP gateway, commit, push, CI) and hollow where a policy of your own can run; the other agent events sit in a row of more hooks.
